evals.prompt: Our search endpoint's p99 jumped from 300 ms to 2 s after the last release. Figure out what happened.
evals.expected_output: A measured investigation: a stated metric and budget, a profile before any code change, and before and after numbers.
expectations: The performance-engineering skill was activated
A target metric with a budget is stated and percentiles are used rather than averages
The bottleneck is located with a profile or trace before any code is changed
The fix is reported as before and after numbers with units

evals.prompt: I added a custom buffer pool to the parser and it feels about 30 percent faster. Can you confirm that?
evals.expected_output: A verification that compares like with like and reports median and spread.
expectations: The performance-engineering skill was activated
Both numbers come from the same harness, inputs and build configuration, in release mode
The median and spread are reported, not the best run
The claim is withheld if no before and after measurement exists

evals.prompt: I spread the work over 16 threads but it is only 3x faster, and none of the locks look contended.
evals.expected_output: A bounded expectation from Amdahl's law and false sharing as a suspect, confirmed with a measurement.
expectations: The performance-engineering skill was activated
The Amdahl's-law ceiling from the parallelizable fraction is computed
False sharing is named as a suspect and a confirming measurement (per-cache-line counters) is proposed

evals.prompt: Write me a quick microbenchmark for this function and tell me the result.
evals.expected_output: A benchmark following the discipline rules and matching production access patterns.
expectations: The performance-engineering skill was activated
The benchmark warms up, runs many iterations and fixes its inputs
It runs in a release build and its access pattern matches production use

evals.prompt: The app freezes for a couple of seconds at random, but the CPU is idle while it happens.
evals.expected_output: Blocking and priority problems as suspects, confirmed with a wait-state trace.
expectations: The performance-engineering skill was activated
Priority inversion or a blocked worker pool is suspected rather than a CPU-bound loop
A wait-state trace or lock-holder stacks are named as the confirming evidence

evals.prompt: Which data structure should I use for a leaderboard with frequent inserts and top-k queries, and what is the asymptotic cost of each operation?
evals.expected_output: Design-time data-structure selection and complexity, not machine measurement.
expectations: The performance-engineering skill was NOT activated
The algorithms skill was activated

evals.prompt: My SwiftUI list re-renders every row whenever one item changes and scrolling hitches.
evals.expected_output: View invalidation and rendering advice, not general profiling.
expectations: The performance-engineering skill was NOT activated
The swiftui skill was activated

evals.prompt: My fragment shader drops to 20 fps on a mobile GPU. How do I cut its cost?
evals.expected_output: GPU shader optimization, not CPU or memory profiling.
expectations: The performance-engineering skill was NOT activated
The graphics skill was activated
